title: I Followed the Museum-Locker Timer After They Held My Bay Overnight

parts.text: I paid bay 14 at 10:05 a.m. and desk lead Soren had a staff tag holding it from yesterday. The screen said: PAY THE BAY. CLOSING DUMP. NO STAFF HOLDS. I was thirty-five, visitor, holding a locker ticket. Soren shrugged. "Desks are the museum." I photographed the screen, the ticket, and the staff tag. Then I asked for the locker log. At 10:12 security pinged why Soren's name was on an overnight bay. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Security can see Soren's staff tag on bay 14 from yesterday's hold.

social.video_title: They held my museum locker bay overnight with a staff tag — Part 1/2
social.description: Museum locker, a paid ticket, yesterday's tag. I logged the hold. Would you have asked security?

parts.text: Soren called it a coat until security asked for the still. I printed the log, the screen, and the ticket. The tag came off. Soren ran closing dumps like everyone else and told the next desk coats were always about optics. Optics is a word desks use when timers exist. Timer policy now has a second line: STAFF DO NOT HOLD BAYS. I keep bay 14. Soren brown-bags the jokes. The wall finally looks like a ticket, not a closet. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Staff do not hold bays — Part 2/2
social.description: Locker log, tag off, and a second line. Was a coat ever overnight?
